B. The reaction rate will decrease by a factor of 2

Thought: I need to analyze how the rate of an SN1 reaction is affected by changing the concentration of a nucleophile (bromide ions in this case).

For an SN1 reaction, the mechanism consists of two steps:
1. The slow, rate-determining step: The leaving group (chloride) departs, forming a carbocation intermediate
2. The fast step: The nucleophile (bromide) attacks the carbocation

The rate law for an SN1 reaction depends only on the concentration of the substrate (tert-butyl chloride in this case), not on the concentration of the nucleophile. This is because the nucleophile is not involved in the rate-determining step.

The rate law would be:
Rate = k[tert-butyl chloride]

Since the concentration of bromide ions does not appear in the rate law, doubling the bromide ion concentration would have no effect on the reaction rate.
